name: Bakery-Style Cream Scones With Milk Chocolate

ingredients.name: all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
cold unsalted butter, cut into 1/2-inch cubes

instructions.primary_message: Adjust oven rack to lower-middle position and preheat to 200°C (400°F). Sift flour into a medium bowl, then whisk in baking powder, sugar, and salt. Add butter and toss to break up the pieces, then smash each one flat between your fingertips. Continue smashing and rubbing until butter disappears into a coarse meal. Add milk chocolate and toss to combine, then stir in milk and cream to form a soft dough.

Turn onto a lightly floured surface and pat into a 18-cm round. Cut into 6 wedges with a chef’s knife, sprinkle generously with toasted or turbinado sugar, and arrange on a parchment-lined half sheet pan. Bake until puffed and golden, about 25 minutes. If you like, serve with clotted cream and strawberry jam, or a spoonful of super-thick and fruity whipped cream.

schema_metadata.keywords: Bake, breakfast, brunch, chocolate, dessert, easy, pastry, quick, scone

description: These super-simple scones are fluffy but crumbly and only lightly sweetened, and come together faster than you can preheat an oven.
notes:
Optional substitutions: Toasted sugar → turbinado sugar

Notes: I love topping these scones with lightly toasted sugar left over from blind-baking a pie, but if you don't have any on hand, turbinado sugar can be used to similar effect.
author: Stella Parks
